Spizella passerina: Compared with Worthen's: both reference birds show a rusty cap, pale breast and brown patterned wings; the Chipping reference has a sharper dark eye stripe. Small reference sample.
Spizella pallida: Compared with Field: both have brown patterned wings, pale underparts and a small conical bill; the Clay-colored reference has a more strongly outlined cheek, while Field shows a pink bill and pale eye ring.
Spizella breweri: Compared with Worthen's: both have slim bodies, long tails, small bills and brown wing markings. Brewer's reference has a more finely patterned head; Worthen's has a plainer gray face.
Spizella pusilla: Compared with Clay-colored: both have pale underparts and brown patterned wings. Field's reference shows a rusty cap and pink bill; Clay-colored shows stronger cheek markings.
Spizella atrogularis: Compared with Worthen's: both show gray faces and pale underparts. The Black-chinned reference shows a darker throat, but the bird is small in the frame, limiting fine-detail comparison.
Spizella wortheni: Compared with Clay-colored: both have pale underparts, brown patterned wings and small bills. Worthen's reference appears grayer and less strongly patterned around the face.
Zonotrichia leucophrys: Compared with Golden-crowned: both have brown patterned wings and pale gray-brown underparts. The White-crowned reference has bold black-and-white crown stripes; Golden-crowned shows a yellow crown patch.
Zonotrichia albicollis: Compared with Golden-crowned: both show brown patterned wings and grayish underparts. The White-throated reference has a conspicuous pale throat; crown details are less clear at this viewing angle.
Zonotrichia querula: Compared with White-crowned: the Harris's reference shows a brown patterned back and sparrow-like silhouette, but is distant and facing away. Head and throat differences cannot be assessed reliably from this photo.
Zonotrichia capensis: Compared with White-throated: both show a patterned head and brown patterned wings. Rufous-collared has a visible rusty collar and stronger dark head stripes in the selected photo.
Zonotrichia atricapilla: Compared with White-crowned: both show brown patterned wings and pale underparts. Their visible crown colors differ: yellow versus broad black-and-white stripes.
Junco hyemalis: Compared with Yellow-eyed: both show compact bodies, conical bills, long tails and gray plumage. The selected Dark-eyed bird has a dark eye and darker head; Yellow-eyed shows a yellow iris and rusty back. Dark-eyed juncos have substantial plumage variation.
Junco phaeonotus: Compared with Dark-eyed: both show gray plumage, compact bodies and long tails. Yellow-eyed has a bright iris and rusty back in this photo; the selected Dark-eyed bird has a dark iris and darker head.
Junco vulcani: Compared with Dark-eyed: both show gray heads, conical bills and compact bodies. Volcano's reference has a yellow eye and more strongly streaked brown upperparts.
Melospiza melodia: Compared with Lincoln's: both references show brown backs, pale eyebrows and dark streaking on pale breasts. Song's streaks appear heavier; Lincoln's photograph is partly obscured by branches.
Melospiza lincolnii: Compared with Song: both show brown plumage and breast streaking. Lincoln's reference has finer visible streaks, although branches and lighting limit the comparison.
Melospiza georgiana: Compared with Song: both have brown wings, patterned heads and long tails. Swamp's reference has warmer rusty wing coloration and less conspicuous breast streaking.
Pipilo erythrophthalmus: Compared with Spotted: both selected birds show dark heads and backs, rusty sides and pale bellies. The Spotted reference has much more conspicuous white spotting on its wings/back.
Pipilo maculatus: Compared with Eastern: both selected birds show dark heads, rusty sides and pale bellies. White spots across the Spotted reference's wings/back provide a clear visual difference.
Pipilo chlorurus: Compared with Spotted: both show a long tail and conical bill, but coloration differs strongly. Green-tailed has olive-yellow wing/tail edges, gray underparts, a white throat and rusty cap; Spotted has a dark head, rusty sides and white wing spots. Same-genus proximity need not imply overall color similarity.
